newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - July 18.

text.p: Analysts predict growth despite flat economy: A welter of economic indicators released this week point to a still flat economy, but analysts are nevertheless picking an upturn later in the year. Page 1.

US government guns for Dairy Board: The Dairy Board has been named number two target in the US Department of Agriculture's war against so-called state trading enterprises it is preparing to wage in the next round of world agricultural trade negotiations. Page 1.

IRD blows time on ailing soccer club: Soccer New Zealand says the game is on a rebuild roll -- but a former top club is partly blaming the cost of playing in the national league for it going to the financial well. Page 5.

Treasure hunter pinpoints success: Delegates at a tourism industry conference in Christchurch today were due to hear about the quest for gold from the wreck of the General Grant, sunk in 1866 at the Auckland Islands. Page 7.

Comalco feels the pain of exchange rates: Comalco (NZ) managing director Kerry McDonald says the Tiwai Pt aluminium smelter has lost about 25 percent of its competitiveness as a result of recent adverse exchange rate changes. Page 9.
Dairy Board braces itself for loss of its monopoly: Powerful forces inside and outside New Zealand are forcing the Dairy Board to rethink its single-desk marketing structure. Page 10.
Shipley fights back: Accident compensation minister Jenny Shipley battled back against accusations from farmers this week that the ACC scheme was ripping them off. Page 11.

Legal scourge attacks Coeur Gold: An aggresive California-based law firm, specialising in squeezing multi-million dollar settlements from high-tech companies, is masterminding the lawsuit filed in the United States earlier this month over Coeur d'Alene's Golden Cross mine near Waihi. Page 1.
Govt bans and backs cheap drug: A cheap imported antibiotic deregistered by the Health Ministry is still being sold to consumers. Page 1.
Meat inspection to go through mincer: Meat producers are cheering moves to give processors greater control of meat inspection are being cautioned not to expect too much from the reforms. Page 2.

Maori tv pursues its missing money: Ill-stared Maori broadcaster Aotearoa Television is investigating the whereabouts of the $150,000 final payment it made for assets of television production company 601 Digital. Page 3.

Pharmac seeks review of patent law: THe government's drugs buying agency Pharmac is seeking a legal review of the law relating to drugs patents after the Commissioner of Patents changed his mind over the handling of them. Page 4.

Best Buy's victims find better deal: Computer buyers left out-of-pocket when Auckland personal computer retailer Best Buy went belly up have switched together a deal with another computer company in a bid to recoup some of their losses. Page 7.
